clue.text: Sponsor heading north saw hammerhead in receding waves

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word heading north is read upwards, so from the bottom letter to the top

blocks.note: to back a venture is to sponsor it
taken as written, then turned upwards
the head of hammer is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A sponsor swimming north spots a hammerhead shark in the waves pulling back from the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: The hammerhead looks like the shark, but it is split: 'head' picks the first letter of hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: Backwash is the water flowing back down a beach after a wave breaks, or behind a moving vessel.

clue.text: The game's up - the sappers have exposed a monster

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word that goes up is read from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: Go is the Japanese board game; read upwards here
RE, the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers

explanation.surface: The game is over: army engineers have unmasked a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The game's up' reads as the idiom for being found out, but it means the game GO turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folk tales, the classic fairy-story monster.

clue.text: Puzzle about a "Dances with Wolves" debut?

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so only the first letter of the name is used

blocks.note: jigs are lively folk dances
taken as written
the first letter of Wolves

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how the Kevin Costner film Dances with Wolves came to be made.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title looks like one unit, but it splits into JIGS, A and W; the quotation marks are only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a picture puzzle cut into interlocking pieces to be fitted back together.

clue.text: Letter from Greece with spare from somewhere in South America?

blocks.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
spare in the sense of thin or lean

explanation.surface: A letter posted from Greece, with something extra from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' looks like extra, but it means thin, lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilean describes a person or thing coming from Chile, a country on the western side of South America.

clue.text: Prior: clergyman in devout environment

indicators.note: one thing in another's environment sits inside it, surrounded on both sides

blocks.note: devout means pious; the environment is the outer shell
Rev, short for Reverend, a clergyman's title

explanation.surface: A monastic prior, a churchman living in a godly setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' looks like a religious title to match the clergyman, but it is the adjective meaning earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Previous and prior both mean coming earlier in time or order.

clue.text: Daunting postponement

blocks.note: first meaning: discouraging, deterring someone
second meaning: delaying something until later

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses use the same phrasal verb: to put someone off is to deter them, to put something off is to delay it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both discouraging a person and deferring a task to a later date.

clue.text: America's first female Attorney General - extremely well-known celebrity

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the phrase, its first and last letters

blocks.note: Janet Reno was the first woman US Attorney General
the outside letters of well-known

explanation.surface: Janet Reno, the first woman to serve as US Attorney General, was a very famous public figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is fame or celebrity, the state of being widely known and admired.

clue.text: Suffering on top of lonesome pine

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: first letter of lonesome
anguish is severe suffering

explanation.surface: Evokes the old song The Trail of the Lonesome Pine, with someone suffering at the top of the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the tree from the song, but it is the verb meaning to waste away with longing.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to pine, wasting away or growing weak from longing or neglect.

clue.text: Galvanised iron core, second-hand

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle, so its central letters are kept

blocks.note: the middle two letters of iron
used goods are second-hand

explanation.surface: A piece of galvanised iron sold second-hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Galvanised iron' reads as one metal, but galvanised is the definition and iron gives its core.
explanation.definitionFit: Galvanised here means stirred into action, spurred or stimulated, as someone roused to act.

clue.text: Isle in south-east Kentucky

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the second item wraps the first

blocks.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east
KY is the postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: An island somewhere in the south-east corner of Kentucky.
explanation.walkthrough: Skye is a large island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the best-known of the Hebridean islands off the Scottish west coast.

clue.text: Mouth-watering mixture of oils in a vat

indicators.note: a mixture blends its ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tempting blend of cooking oils in a big vat.
explanation.walkthrough: Mouth-watering is read as a noun here, the watering of the mouth, not the adjective for tasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Salivation is the production of spit, literally the watering of the mouth.

clue.text: Immature beast has everything

indicators.note: something that has another thing holds it, so one word is held inside the other

blocks.note: a cow is a farm beast
all means everything

explanation.surface: A young animal that has everything it could want.
explanation.definitionFit: Callow describes someone young and inexperienced, lacking adult maturity.

clue.text: Complaint making poor girl stay in

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are taken as damaged and rearranged

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An illness that keeps an unfortunate girl at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' is the medical sense, an ailment, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Laryngitis is an inflammation of the voice box, a minor illness or ailment.

clue.text: Trouble with sailors taking in grand decking

blocks.note: ado is fuss or trouble
RN, the Royal Navy
taken as written
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Sailors cause trouble by bringing a grand piano onto the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decking' suggests a ship's deck to go with the sailors, but it is the verb deck, to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a room is to adorn it with decorations, so decking and adorning are synonyms.

clue.text: Sausage from Spain, Switzerland or Italy (about an ounce)

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so these letters face the other way

blocks.note: CH is Switzerland's international vehicle code
taken as written
I is Italy's international vehicle code
oz is the abbreviation for ounce

explanation.surface: Asking where a sausage comes from: Spain, Switzerland or Italy, sold by the ounce.
explanation.definitionFit: Chorizo is a spicy pork sausage flavoured with paprika, a Spanish speciality.

clue.text: Love and honour - not on time for action

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the following word from the one before

blocks.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis
taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Love and honour are not on time when it comes to action.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero because it is the tennis score for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero hour is the moment set for a military operation or other planned event to begin.

clue.text: Surprise about German connection

blocks.note: as to means about, concerning
und is German for and, a connecting word

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised about a link with Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Connection' means a connecting word, a conjunction, not a link between people.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound someone is to surprise or amaze them greatly.

clue.text: Gratuitous indicators on top of screen

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, which is kept

blocks.note: needles are the pointers on dials and gauges
first letter of screen

explanation.surface: Unnecessary pointers placed over a display screen.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, NEEDLES sits on top of S.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratuitous means uncalled-for or unnecessary, without good reason, which is what needless means.

clue.text: Doctor with duck in northern stream revealing what is fundamental

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: beck is a northern English word for a brook; it wraps the rest
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A doctor with a duck wading in a northern brook finds the basic truth.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is O because a cricketer out for no runs scores a duck; both the doctor and the duck go inside the stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrock is the solid rock under soil, and figuratively the basic principles everything rests on.

clue.text: Don's role - translating a dead language

indicators.note: translating turns words into another form, so these letters are recast in a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A university lecturer's job is translating an ancient tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university teacher, which makes translating feel literal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse is the medieval Scandinavian tongue of the Vikings, no longer spoken.

clue.text: Kylie in Sydney Harbour stays in bed

indicators.note: to harbour something is to shelter it, so the words keep the answer tucked inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of Kylie, all of in and the start of Sydney

explanation.surface: The singer Kylie Minogue lazes in bed on a boat in Sydney Harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sydney Harbour' looks like a place name, but Harbour is the instruction to look inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Lie-ins are mornings spent staying in bed later than usual; stays is read as a plural noun.

clue.text: Distant cardinal, out of tune

blocks.note: off can mean far away, distant
cardinal means chief or principal, as does key

explanation.surface: A remote churchman who cannot sing in tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a prince of the church, but here it is the adjective meaning chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-key describes singing or playing at the wrong pitch, not matching the correct note.

clue.text: One has grasped nothing about being connected to the network

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so this word is read backwards
something that has grasped another holds it inside

blocks.note: taken as written; it holds the rest
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone has got nowhere in trying to get on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One has grasped nothing' reads as a failure, but it is an instruction to put a word for nothing inside one.
explanation.definitionFit: Online means linked to a computer network such as the internet.

clue.text: Quiet goddess in jeopardy on the fringe

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: jeopardy is danger, peril; it holds the rest
p is piano, the musical marking for quiet
Hera was queen of the Greek gods

explanation.surface: A silent goddess is in danger at the edge of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the quiet letter and the goddess go inside the word for jeopardy, together.
explanation.definitionFit: Peripheral means situated at the edge or outer boundary, away from the centre.

clue.text: Art going to droop?

blocks.note: first meaning: old second-person verb form, as in thou art going to
second meaning: to sag or wither, as a plant without water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' looks like painting, but it is the archaic 'thou art'; 'thou wilt' means thou will, so 'art going to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilt is the old form of will used with thou, and also means to sag or wither.

clue.text: Christopher's ending in novel about architect

indicators.note: the ending of a name is its last letter, which is kept
about can mean turned round, so this word is read backwards
one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: last letter of Christopher
novel means new; it is turned round and holds the letter

explanation.surface: The end of a novel about the architect Christopher.
explanation.walkthrough: NEW turned round gives WEN, with R inside. The surface name points straight to the answer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren was the English architect who designed St Paul's Cathedral in London.

clue.text: What examinees do between home and university is not out of place

indicators.note: something between two others sits inside the pair, flanked on either side

blocks.note: in means at home
candidates sit an exam
U is short for university

explanation.surface: Students taking exams between home and university are where they should be.
explanation.definitionFit: In situ is Latin for in its original place, so not moved or displaced.

clue.text: Talk about 22 down?

blocks.note: c, circa, means about
22 down reads ON-LINE, and a line of poetry is a verse

explanation.surface: A request to chat about the answer to another clue in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 22 down splits into ON and LINE, and LINE is swapped for its synonym VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to talk with someone, to hold a conversation.
